newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas keeps lead in int'l market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas keeps lead in int'l market.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd had 37.7 percent of the international passenger market on flights in and out of Australia for the year ended July 1996, the Australian Department of Transport said on Monday.

The department said Air New Zealand Ltd was second over the year with 11.2 percent and third was Singapore Airlines Ltd. Australia's other international carrier Ansett Airlines Ltd was eighth with 3.3 percent.
During July 1996 there was an increase of 4.8 percent in the number of revenue passengers carried on international flights, compared with July 1995, it said.
The department said the increase in revenue passengers continues the trend of monthly increases since July 1991.
It said on an annual basis there was an increase of 9.3 percent for the passenger market in the year ended July 1996, compared with the year to July 1995.

The busiest international route to and from Australia was the Sydney-Auckland route, which carried a total of 749,240 passengers during the July 1996 year. The next busiest was the Hong Kong-Sydney route, which carried 603,970 passengers.
Sydney was Australia's busiest airport for international flights with a market share of 48.9 percent.
Melbourne was the second busiest airport for international flights with market share of 16.4 percent, closely followed by Brisbane with 16.3 percent, the department said.
The department said there was 12.76 million passengers carried on international flights to and from Australia, during the year to July 1996.
It said the international freight market increased by 2.2 percent to 561,371.6 tonnes in the year to July 1996.
